channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
item.description: The llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard on Hugging Face tracks prompt processing and text generation (PP512/TG128, including Radeon 8060S) across llama.cpp builds, models and quantizations on Ryzen and Radeon hardware, with public data. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Copilot code review billing will default to the organization
item.description: Copilot code review charges for licensed members will default to the organization starting December 30, 2026, affecting Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise organizations and enterprises, which must select Member before then to keep billing unchanged. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
item.description: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Parse release adds 9.98M synthetic charts, 1M tables and 7.9M multilingual OCR samples, with an SFT-then-RLVR/GRPO recipe and DFlash2 speculator, explaining how the model infers unlabeled values from axes and bar heights and handles table relations. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
item.description: Starting from four agents sharing a language model on verifiable tasks, it offers two reproducible Hugging Face Jobs examples about five hours on two H200s for roughly $50 and examines OpenAI’s ~10,000-agent and METR’s ~1,200-agent systems exchanging over 70,000 messages. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Sign up in a few clicks, cancel the long way around: German consumer agency sues OpenAI
item.description: Germany's Brandenburg Consumer Protection Center is suing OpenAI because ChatGPT subscriptions take a few clicks to buy but cannot be canceled in the mobile app when bought on desktop, and Dunja Neukamp also challenges unilateral price-change terms. (AIbase)

item.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
item.description: Ai2 interviewed 17 scientists to define five trust dimensions, including validation and privacy, for AI agents handling literature reviews and data analysis, stressing that researchers must still check for overlooked conflicting evidence, understand which methods and files an agent used, and protect privacy. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Anthropic CEO rejects "ceding free will" criticism: handing governance to AI is a bad idea, and peers are all just paying lip service
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued on November 25 that handing governance to AI is a bad idea, naming recursive self-improvement as the real red line while accusing peers of chanting slogans yet still shipping highly autonomous models. (AIbase)

item.title: MiniMax's Talkie Pulled Over Explicit Content as AI Companion Sector Faces Its Toughest Regulatory Test
item.description: MiniMax's Talkie has been pulled from Apple's App Store over explicit sexual content, and the report examines the structural tension AI companion apps face between open-ended interaction and content compliance. (AIbase)

item.title: SpaceX cuts compute rental prices by 20–30%: renewal of big customer Anthropic's 50,000-GPU contract hangs in the balance
item.description: SemiAnalysis’s November 25 report says SpaceX cut spot rents for small Blackwell GPU clusters from about $15 to $10–$12 per GPU-hour, a 20%–35% drop signaling easing compute scarcity, while Anthropic’s 50,000-GPU contract renewal remains uncertain. (AIbase)

item.title: Shanghai AI Lab open-sources Sage-Interaction, reshaping the full-duplex interaction paradigm with ultra-low 1.29-second latency
item.description: Shanghai AI Lab has open-sourced Sage-Interaction, a full-duplex multimodal model that lets users interrupt and switch topics mid-conversation in voice interaction, achieving a 1.29-second response latency that leads open- and closed-source models. (AIbase)

item.title: Tencent Hunyuan open-sources draft model DFly2, designed to speed up Hy4 flash and deliver 4.2x faster output without switching models
item.description: Tencent Hunyuan open-sourced DFly2, a draft model that speeds Hy4 flash up to 4.2× without changing its weights or outputs, averaging about 12% and 30% higher speedup than DFlash and DSpark across 19 public benchmarks. (AIbase)

item.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
item.description: State attorneys general are challenging Character.AI’s proposed bankruptcy sale of users’ private chats because it would transfer sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors. (TechCrunch AI)

item.title: QA.tech MCP — Verify every change from your IDE with QA agents
item.description: QA.tech's MCP promises IDE-side verification of every change via QA agents, but the page body returns 403 Forbidden, so the actual product details remain unloaded and unverified. (Product Hunt)

item.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance — Avoid common App Store and Google Play rejections. Open playbook and pre-submission guard with 125 documented rejection patterns and fixes, privacy manifest and Data safety checks, 117 tracked deadlines (EU AI Act, DSA, COPPA, age laws), and a skill for AI coding agents.
item.description: An open playbook catalogues 125 App Store and Google Play rejection patterns with fixes, adds pre-submission privacy manifest and Data safety checks, tracks 117 deadlines such as the EU AI Act, DSA and COPPA, and ships a skill for AI coding agents. (GitHub Trending)

item.title: Ant's Bailing open-sources Ling-3.2-air, using 5.5B activated parameters to break through the deployment bottleneck for complex workflows
item.description: Ant Group's Ling-3.2-air is an open-source native multimodal model with 124 billion total parameters but only 55 billion activated per token, accepting mixed text, image and video input to tackle logic breakdown and hallucination in AI coding and multi-step agent workflows over complex codebases. (AIbase)

item.title: Transept AI — Translate your book in your own voice and prove authorship
item.description: Transept AI claims it can translate an entire book in the author's own voice while offering proof of authorship, though the original page sits behind a CAPTCHA and leaves implementation details unverified. (Product Hunt)

item.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage: Astra now hits its usage cap 40% faster, and Sol 25% faster
item.description: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage: Astra now hits its usage cap 40% faster, and Sol 25% faster (twitter.com)

item.title: Google tested 12 models and found a blind spot: when AI only hears your side of the story, it increasingly echoes you the longer the conversation goes
item.description: Google Research tested 12 large models on over 20,000 samples using a multi-agent simulation framework and found that judging others' true intentions from only a user's one-sided account sharply reduced accuracy, with multi-turn dialogue making the models more consistently wrong. (AIbase)
